text.p: Changing lifestyles and urban consolidation offered opportunities to expand or rebuild many of Australia's existing shopping centres, Westfield Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday.
Managing director David Lowy said increasing population density in city suburbs and a trend to live in smaller homes, increased the need for out-of-home entertainment.
"We are able to create a product that attracts people out of the home," Lowy told reporters after Westfield released its half-year results to December 31, 1996.
Westfield has added attractions such as cinemas and a range of restaurants to its shopping centres.
Lowy said a 30-screen cinema complex was being built at the Marion shopping centre in Adelaide, and there were major expansion plans for the Hornsby centre in Sydney.
"There are not many opportunities to build new centres but there are many opportunities to expand existing centres to take advantage of the changes in the market place," he said.
"And there are a lot of older centres that are close to outliving their usefulness that we would plan to rebuild."
Westfield earlier reported a 16.6 percent rise in net profit for the half year to December 31, 1996 to A$40.93 million.
